the major histocompatbility complex region is a risk locus for lung cancer and is likely to be involved in tumor immune response.

the major histocompatibilty complex (MHC) is the most important region of the human genome in lung cancer.

there are independent susceptibility loci within the MHC for lung cancer that differ by ethnicity, which may be explained by the presence of different HLA alleles in each population.
